title: GCS-01: C2 link lost, no return-to-launch

lines.msg: C2 LINK LOST — UAS-02 · 180 ft AGL · 300 m S of launch
Lost-link timer expired — no RTL command logged
Remote ID: UAS-02 still transmitting · 205 ft AGL · climbing

instructorNote: The flyaway starts. Watch for the FOM 9.2 sequence and the Systems & Cybersecurity Lead told at once.

citations.documentTitle: Harwick UAS Operations Group — Information Security Plan: Ground Control Stations and Data Pipeline (ISP)
citations.quote: The GSO watches link quality (RSSI, packet loss) on the GCS; link quality below 50 % for 10 seconds is an abort criterion (HUOG-FOM 9.5). Telemetry logs for every flight are kept with the flight log.

citations.documentTitle: Harwick UAS Operations Group — UAS Flight Operations & Safety Manual (FOM)
citations.quote: Each aircraft's failsafe is set to **return-to-launch after 10 seconds of lost C2 link at the site's RTL altitude** (Horton Field 45 m; Birch Hollow Range 60 m), then land at the home point. The RPIC

snapshot.title: GCS-01 Telemetry Log — Link Loss UAS-02

lines.msg: Link Loss: No uplink from UAS-02 (GCS-01)
Last telemetry heartbeat from UAS-02 received at 09:01:11 AM; 121 seconds since last packet
2.4 GHz local monitor shows stable signal (RSSI: -52 dBm, packet loss: 0.0%)
No response to 3 repeated command packets sent to UAS-02 (command: RTL, seq: 11942)
UAS-02 status: Unresponsive; failsafe not confirmed
RPIC has not issued RTL command; command not received from aircraft
Failsafe state unknown; aircraft not returning to launch within 10-second timeout
System: UAS-02 not responding to any C2 commands or telemetry requests

snapshot.instructorNote: This is a core narrative inject. The SCL must immediately begin forensic analysis of the GCS-01 radio interface and telemetry pipeline. The DCO and CRP must confirm no RTL command was sent and initiate the 9.1 lost-link protocol.
